Приехал мужик из села в отпуск на море. Лежит, загорает.На пляже подходит к нему симпатичная женщина и говорит:
- Мне так скучно, одиноко. Не составите мне компанию?
Мужик:
- Нет проблем!
Пошли они в ресторан, отметили знакомство, выпили. В итоге попали в номер к даме. Дама приняла душ и начала приставать к мужику, а он говорит, что у него не стоит. Она говорит, что это она решит. Берет баночку со сметаной и намазывает мужику член, потом зовет пуделька и приказывает полизать член. Член встает, и мужик хорошо отдирает даму.
И так весь отпуск.
Приезжает мужик в село, открывает ворота и кричит жене:
- Марфа, готовся, ебать буду!
Жена:
- Так у тебя же не стоит.
Мужик:
- Давай сметану и зови Бобика!
Дала она ему сметану. Он достает член, мокает его в сметану и показывает Бобику. Бобик посмотрел на член, посмотрел на хозяина, а потом взял и откусил член.
Мужик:
- Ну село есть село!

🇪🇸❌ Spain moves to shut Palantir out of the state — the spy-tech empire hits another European wall

Spain’s Prime Minister’s Office has reportedly instructed public companies and administrations to avoid contracts with the US surveillance-tech giant Palantir Technologies over concerns about national sovereignty and sensitive security information, El Periódico reported.

💬 The message from Madrid is blunt: avoid “any contract with Palantir Technologies that could put national sovereignty at risk.”

This is not just a procurement story.

It is another sign that European governments are beginning to understand what Palantir actually represents: not a neutral software vendor, but a CIA-seeded, US-linked data empire embedded in intelligence, policing, migration control, military AI and public infrastructure.

Spain is now moving in the same direction as France and Germany.

🇫🇷 France selected domestic company ChapsVision to replace Palantir in its internal intelligence service, with officials arguing that sensitive national data must be stored and processed inside the country.

🇩🇪 Germany’s military cyber leadership also rejected Palantir for now, saying the company does not meet certain requirements of the German armed forces.

And then there is Palantir’s record.

The company was founded in 2003 with early backing from the CIA’s In-Q-Tel investment arm. Its platforms have been used by US ICE and DHS in immigration tracking and deportation-related work, drawing criticism from Amnesty International, the ACLU and the Electronic Frontier Foundation over privacy and rights concerns.

It has also moved deeper into the military sphere, including a strategic partnership with Israel’s Ministry of Defense during the Gaza war and a major role in Pentagon AI programs such as Maven Smart System.

Palantir’s defenders say the company only provides software and that clients control the data.

Critics see something far darker: infrastructure for large-scale surveillance and control.

And that is the core issue.

Once Palantir enters a state system, it does not just “provide tools.” It creates dependency. It sits near the data. It shapes how police, militaries, ministries, hospitals and intelligence agencies see the world.

Spain appears to have noticed the trap before it becomes permanent.

☠️ Palantir’s empire is built on one promise: give us the data, and we will make the state more powerful.

Europe is starting to ask the obvious question:

👀 Powerful for whom?
